title: Lead workflow engine: operations, legality matrix, status history, pricing approvals, follow-ups
objective: All twelve lead workflow operations from PRD 10.4 execute as commands with legality validation, op-specific inputs, append-only status history, audit, and availableOperations exposure (spec FR-34..FR-37, FR-40..FR-42, §9.2).
scope: LeadWorkflow legality matrix keyed on canonical_key/reporting category

Operation commands: Assign/Reassign, StartInformationGathering, SendToUnderwriting, StartPricing, RequestPricingApproval, ApprovePricing, RejectPricing, LogFollowUp, StartNegotiation, MarkLeadLost, WithdrawLead, ReopenLead
out_of_scope: Quote operations and cascades' quote side (T-020 implements IQuoteCascadeService)
implementation_details: Liquibase 100-lead-workflow: lead_status_history (tenant_id, id, lead_id, operation text, previous_status_id, new_status_id, acted_by, acted_at, inputs jsonb); pricing_approvals per spec §11.3; follow_ups (tenant_id, id, lead_id, follow_up_date date, outcome_note text, next_follow_up_date date null, logged_by, logged_at)

Domain/Workflow/LeadWorkflow.cs: static legality matrix Dictionary<LeadOperation, OperationRule{AllowedFrom(canonical keys or categories), Target(canonical key or 'unchanged')}> transcribed exactly from PRD 10.4 lead table; statuses resolved via reference_items canonical_key; tenant-added intermediate statuses inherit their reporting category's operation set; pure and unit-testable

Application/Features/Leads/Workflow/: one command+validator+handler per operation; shared LeadOperationExecutor: load lead (tenant-filtered), check legality (409 ILLEGAL_TRANSITION with legal ops hint), check permission (per-op permission map, e.g. pricing approve/reject -> Pricing.Approve; Reopen -> Leads.Reopen), apply mutation + side effects, append history row with inputs jsonb, audit, enqueue alert re-evaluation hook (IAlertReevaluationQueue no-op until T-024)

AssignLead: payload {assignments:[{businessAssignmentId, userId|null}], comment?}; accountable owner required non-null; upserts lead_assignments; New -> Assigned sets date_assigned; reassign keeps status; history inputs record per-role previous/new
SendToUnderwriting: {underwritingOwnerUserId, note?} -> sets underwriting-role assignment + status underwriting; underwriting SLA clock = history timestamp

RequestPricingApproval: {approverUserId (must hold Pricing.Approve), proposedPremium?, note?} -> pricing_approvals row state pending, lead.pricing_approval_state=pending; ApprovePricing {note?} / RejectPricing {rejectionReason required} permission-bound, only by/for pending request; rejection allows re-request

LogFollowUp: {followUpDate default today, outcomeNote, nextFollowUpDate} -> nextFollowUpDate required and future when lead open past quote_sent (category quoted); inserts follow_ups, updates lead last/next follow-up + follow_up_count; no status change

MarkLeadLost: {lostReasonId required active LostReason, competitor?, competitorPremium?, lossComments (required when reason canonical 'other')} -> status closed_lost, decision_date, lost_before_quote computed (no quote ever sent), calls IQuoteCascadeService.CascadeLeadLost(leadId); WithdrawLead {withdrawalNote required} -> withdrawn + CascadeLeadWithdrawn; ReopenLead {reopenReason required} permission-bound -> returns to last open/quoted status from history (A-13)
AvailableOperationsCalculator: legality matrix ∩ caller permissions -> string[] on GetLead DTO; used by UI to hide illegal actions (FR-17)

findings.description: The SendToUnderwriting role-assignment side effect (required by AC-035 'side effects match PRD 10.4 exactly' + FR-36 'sets underwriting role') is entirely UNVERIFIED, and the test name misrepresents coverage. LeadWorkflowTestContext.SeedAccountableOwnerAsync configures NO underwriting-named role, so SendToUnderwritingCommandHandler's underwritingRole lookup resolves null, the assignment/eligibility branch is dead in the test, and SendToUnderwriting_ShouldSetRoleAndStatus asserts only StatusCanonicalKey=='underwriting'. Both the 'underwrit' heuristic match path AND the InvalidAssignee eligibility-rejection (422) path have zero coverage. The heuristic DESIGN itself is accepted as a documented interim (no IsUnderwritingOwner marker exists - a T-011 schema follow-up); this finding is the missing verification of the required side effect.
findings.recommendation: Add an integration test that configures a lead-assignable role whose name contains 'underwrit', asserts a LeadAssignment row IS written for that role after SendToUnderwriting, AND asserts an ineligible underwritingOwnerUserId returns 422. If exercising the now-live branch reveals a code defect, fix it. Rename/scope the existing test honestly.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit). Two new tests genuinely exercise the previously-dead branch and would catch a break: positive (SendToUnderwriting_WhenUnderwritingRoleConfigured_ShouldAssignUnderwritingOwnerAndSetStatus) seeds a BusinessAssignment AppliesTo=lead role named 'Underwriter' matching the RoleName.Contains('underwrit') heuristic, makes a user eligible for THAT role via AddEligibleOwnerAsync(underwritingRole.RoleId), and asserts a lead_assignments row exists by BusinessAssignmentId==underwritingRole.AssignmentId (distinct from the accountable-owner assignment) with UserId==underwriterId - would fail if the assignment weren't persisted (guards the side effect, not the DTO); negative (SendToUnderwriting_WhenUnderwritingOwnerIneligible_ShouldReturn422) seeds the role with no eligible user + passes the accountable-owner as underwritingOwnerUserId -> 422 LEAD_WORKFLOW_INVALID_ASSIGNEE via the genuine eligibility-rejection path (not an earlier guard). Old test renamed SendToUnderwriting_ShouldSetStatusWhenNoUnderwritingRoleConfigured (graceful-degrade, assertion kept, honestly named). No-production-code-change claim VERIFIED TRUE by file mtimes (only the 2 test files touched); the handler branch is correct as designed, no defect. Evaluator re-ran the 2 tests by name -> pass.

findings.description: RejectPricing 'reason required -> 422' (a V-036 negative) has no integration coverage. RejectPricingValidator enforces it (unit-safe) but no API test exercises the 422.
findings.evidence: RejectPricingValidator.cs:10; no RejectPricing_WithoutReason test in LeadWorkflowTests.cs.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2. RejectPricing_WithoutReason_ShouldReturn422 added: moves the lead to Pricing, opens a genuine pending approval, rejects with rejectionReason=null -> 422; approver granted Pricing.Approve/Reject/Leads.View (legitimate separate-approver setup, not a weakening). With a pending request + permitted approver, the null-reason validation is the only failure path. Evaluator re-ran by name -> pass.

findings.description: Two housekeeping/advisory items: (a) BusinessAssignment has no IsUnderwritingOwner structural marker, forcing SendToUnderwriting to use a fragile case-insensitive 'underwrit' role-name substring match - a real marker on the business_assignments schema is a good follow-up (T-011 territory); (b) a stray empty directory 'src/api/db;C' exists (untracked, benign shell-artifact) that should be removed.
findings.evidence: SendToUnderwritingCommandHandler.cs role-name match; stray src/api/db;C directory.
findings.recommendation: Track IsUnderwritingOwner as a T-011/schema follow-up; remove the stray directory during this fix. Non-blocking.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2. Stray src/api/db;C directory removed (not found anywhere under src/api). No IsUnderwritingOwner marker added - BusinessAssignment still carries only IsAccountableOwner; the only 'IsUnderwritingOwner' reference is the handler XML doc comment naming the deferred T-011 follow-up. CARRIED FORWARD: add an IsUnderwritingOwner (or equivalent structural role-purpose marker) to business_assignments in a future T-011 schema pass so SendToUnderwriting no longer relies on the case-insensitive 'underwrit' role-name substring match.
